general.a1: Smart Property is a Tunisian real-estate platform focused on buying, selling, and renting properties only in Tunisia.
general.q2: What property types are available on Smart Property?
general.a2: You can find apartments, houses, villas, studios, and selected commercial opportunities located in Tunisia.
general.q3: How does Smart Property support buyers and renters?
general.a3: Our platform helps you search verified listings in Tunisia, compare options, contact owners or agencies, and follow your process step by step.

buying.q1: How do I start buying a property in Tunisia?
buying.a1: Start by defining your budget in TND, selecting the city/zone, then contacting the listing owner or agency to arrange visits and document checks.
buying.q2: What upfront costs should I plan for?
buying.a2: Plan for a reservation amount (if requested), notary fees, registration fees, and potential bank financing costs based on your profile.
buying.q3: Should I inspect the property before purchase?
buying.a3: Yes. Always verify construction condition, utilities, neighborhood access, and legal documentation before signing final contracts.

selling.q1: What is the best time to sell a property in Tunisia?
selling.a1: Demand often increases around key relocation periods and summer months, but a well-priced property can sell all year in active Tunisian cities.
selling.q2: Should I renovate before listing on Smart Property?
selling.a2: Light improvements like paint, cleaning, and fixing visible defects can improve value perception and speed up buyer interest.
selling.q3: How should I set my selling price?
selling.a3: Use comparable listings in the same Tunisian area, property condition, total surface, and recent market activity to define a realistic TND price.

renting.q1: What documents are usually needed to rent in Tunisia?
renting.a1: Usually: national ID or passport, proof of income, and any guarantor documents required by the owner or agency.
renting.q2: What is usually included in monthly rent?
renting.a2: Monthly rent generally covers occupancy only. Utilities, syndic fees, and maintenance terms should be clearly confirmed in the lease.
renting.q3: How long is a standard lease in Tunisia?
renting.a3: Many residential leases are set for 12 months, with renewal conditions defined in the contract.

legal.q1: What ownership document should I verify?
legal.a1: Always verify the official ownership document (titre foncier or equivalent legal proof) before payment or signature.
legal.q2: Do I need legal supervision during the transaction?
legal.a2: Yes. It is strongly recommended to proceed with legal supervision (notary/lawyer) to secure documents, payments, and transfer steps.
legal.q3: What taxes or fees may apply?
legal.a3: Applicable fees can include registration duties, notary costs, and other legal charges depending on the property and transaction type.

financial.q1: How does home financing work in Tunisia?
financial.a1: A housing loan from a Tunisian bank helps finance your property purchase in TND and is repaid through monthly installments with bank-defined terms.
financial.q2: What are closing fees in Tunisia?
financial.a2: Closing fees may include notary fees, registration charges, and administrative costs due at final transaction signature.
financial.q3: Can first-time buyers get guidance on Smart Property?
financial.a3: Yes. Smart Property helps first-time buyers compare listings, understand required steps, and connect with professionals for legal and financing guidance.
